card.statement:
(5) and so, $\dim\mathscr{A}_{W}(\mathbf{m},\mathbf{n})=1$ by Proposition 7.1 (6). We will give a direct construction of the category ${\mathscr{A}_{W}(D(\ell))}$.

We shall keep the notation

$\ell=(\beta,\gamma),\qquad\beta=(\beta_{1},\ldots,\beta_{p})\in\Bbbk^{p},\qquad\gamma=(\gamma_{1},\ldots,\gamma_{2p})\in\Bbbk^{2p}.$

Since $\ell\in\mathcal{P}_{1}$ then $\beta_{i}-\beta_{j}\notin\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt$ for $i\neq j$. Consider the following category $K_{\ell}$: ${\rm Ob}\,(K_{\ell})=\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt^{p}$ and the morphisms are generated by

$f_{i}(k):(k)\mapsto(k+\delta_{i})\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_{i}(k):(k)\mapsto(k-\delta_{i}),$

where $i=1,\ldots,p$ and $(k)=(k_{1},\ldots,k_{p})\in\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt^{p}$ with the following relations:

$\displaystyle f_{j}(k+\delta_{i})\,f_{i}(k)$ $\displaystyle=f_{i}(k+\delta_{j})\,f_{j}(k),$

$\displaystyle e_{j}(k-\delta_{i})\,e_{i}(k)$ $\displaystyle=e_{i}(k-\delta_{j})\,e_{j}(k),$

$\displaystyle e_{i}(k+\delta_{j})\,f_{j}(k)$ $\displaystyle=f_{j}(k-\delta_{i})\,e_{i}(k)\qquad\text{for}\quad i\neq j,$

$\displaystyle e_{i}(k+\delta_{i})\,f_{i}(k)$ $\displaystyle=-\gamma(-\beta_{i}-k_{i})\,1_{(k)},$

$\displaystyle f_{i}(k-\delta_{i})\,e_{i}(k)$ $\displaystyle=-\gamma(-\beta_{i}-k_{i}+1)\,1_{(k)}.$

It follows immediately from Lemmas 4.1 and 4.3 that any module in the category $R_{\ell}$ can be naturally viewed as a module over the category $K_{\ell}$ which defines a functor $F:R_{\ell}\rightarrow K_{\ell}\text{-mod}$. Consider the cyclic subalgebra $C_{\ell}(a)={\rm Hom}_{K_{\ell}}(a,a)$ for any $a\in\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt^{p}$. Clearly, $C_{\ell}(a)\simeq\Bbbk$ for any $a\in\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt^{p}$ due to the defining relations of $K_{\ell}$. For any $a=(k_{1},\ldots,k_{p})\in\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt^{p}$ we can construct a universal module $M(\ell,a)\in K_{\ell}\text{-mod}$. Consider $\Bbbk$ as a $C_{\ell}(a)$ -module with

$\displaystyle e_{i}(k+\delta_{i})\,f_{i}(k)\,1$ $\displaystyle=-\gamma(-\beta_{i}-k_{i}),$

$\displaystyle f_{i}(k-\delta_{i})\,e_{i}(k)\,1$ $\displaystyle=-\gamma(-\beta_{i}-k_{i}+1).$

Let $A_{\ell,a}$ be an algebra of paths in $K_{\ell}$ originating in $a$. Now construct a $\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt^{p}$ -graded $K_{\ell}$ -module

$M(\ell,a)=A_{\ell,a}\otimes_{C_{\ell}(a)}\Bbbk.$

Clearly, all graded components of $M(\ell,a)$ are $1$ -dimensional and $M(\ell,a)_{a}=1_{a}\otimes\Bbbk$. A module $M(\ell,a)$ contains a unique maximal $\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt^{p}$ -graded submodule which intersects $M(\ell,a)_{a}$ trivially and hence has a unique irreducible quotient $L(\ell,a)$ with $L(\ell,a)_{a}\simeq\Bbbk$ and $\dim L(\ell,a)_{b}\leq 1$ for all $b\in\mathbb{Z}\hskip 1.0pt^{p}$. If $V$ is another irreducible $K_{\ell}$ -module with $V_{a}\neq 0$ then there exists a non-trivial $C_{\ell}(a)$ -homomorphism from $\Bbbk$ to $V_{a}$ which can be extended to an epimorphism from $M(\ell,a)$ to $V$. Since $V$ is irreducible we conclude that $V\simeq L(\ell,a)$.

Obviously, we can view $M(\ell)$ as a module over the category $K_{\ell}$ with a natural action of the morphisms of $K_{\ell}$ and $F(M(\ell))=M(\ell,\beta)$. Thus a $K_{\ell}$ -module $M(\ell,\beta)$ can be extended to a ${\rm Y}_{p}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$ -module $M(\ell)$. Moreover, the functor $F$ preserves the submodule structure of $M(\ell)$. In particular, $F(L(\ell))=L(\ell,\beta)$.
card.label: Proposition 7.1

paper.title: Harish-Chandra modules for Yangians
paper.abstract: We study Harish-Chandra representations of Yangian for gl(2). We prove an analogue of Kostant theorem showing that resterited Yangians for gl(2) are free modules over certain maximal commutative subalgebras. We also study the categories of generic Harish-Chandra modules, describe their simple modules and indecomposable modules in tame blocks.
